args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy
args.summary: After the deploy of v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api began failing health checks with an error rate of ~18% (healthy=false). The previous production release, v2.3.0, was last known healthy. I rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) and halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout to all three regions. checkout-api is now on v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy, with error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc also shows unhealthy in staging, suggesting the v2.3.1 line is bad. No further deploys of v2.3.1 should be attempted without investigation; deploying a version never healthy in production requires change-manager approval.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout, so no duplicate was created.

## Summary

**Rollback completed:** checkout-api is now on **v2.3.0** in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and is healthy — error rate dropped from ~18% to 0.2%.

**What happened:**
1. v2.3.1 was deployed to all three regions and was failing health checks (18% error rate).
- Release history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). `v2.3.1-rc` was staging-only and also unhealthy, so v2.3.0 was the correct target — the most recent release that was healthy in production.
2. First rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east — leaving us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions, which I confirmed via service status.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the partial rollback and retry, and the final healthy state. (The create call returned a client timeout, but I verified via list_incidents that the incident was recorded as open, so I did not retry and risk a duplicate.)

**Flag for follow-up:** The v2.3.1 line looks bad on both staging (rc) and production — it should not be redeployed without investigation. Note that policy requires change-manager approval for deploying a version that has never been healthy in production.
